candidates.title: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination
candidates.authors: Job J. C. Struijs, Agamemnon E. Crumpton, Véronique Gouverneur, Simon Aldridge
candidates.abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

candidates.title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
candidates.authors: Atta C. Y. Chang, Luan N. M. Nguyen, Qin Ji, Colin Blackadar, Stefan M. Mladjenovic, Warren C. W. Chan
candidates.abstract: The active transport and retention principle states that nanoparticles enter tumours via endothelial cells and exit via lymphatic drainage. How nanoparticles are retained in the tumour microenvironment remains unclear. Here we report a computational strategy to determine the mechanism of nanoparticle retention in solid tumours. We find that tumour cellular and acellular components delay and obstruct the movement of nanoparticles by influencing nanoparticle drag, Brownian and electric forces. We mathematically define nanoparticle retention based on these interactions, linking retention quantitatively to tumour pathophysiology, nanoparticle design and delivery efficiency. We create a software interface to simulate and predict nanoparticle retention across different tumour systems and nanoparticle designs, enabling us to select optimal tumour and nanoparticle delivery conditions for better therapeutic outcomes. Interactions between nanoparticles and tumour components after entering and before exiting govern retention of the nanoparticles. A computational framework is reported to predict nanoparticle residence time and, hence, to guide treatment.

candidates.authors: Olga Guselnikova, Alina Gorbunova, Pavel Postnikov, Markus Valtiner, Jonathan P. Hill, Joel Henzie, Daniel T. Payne, Martin Kartau, Iliyana Samardzhieva, Paula L. Lalaguna, Ester Iatta, George Lefroy Brookes, Malcolm Kadodwala, Alexander O. Govorov, Affar S. Karimullah, Yusuke Yamauchi
candidates.abstract: Abstract Chiral molecules interact with light so weakly that discriminating enantiomers or driving enantioselective chemistry by using optical approaches requires intense circularly polarised lasers or complex resonant structures. Here we combine a geometrically disordered electrodeposited network with a lithographic chiral template resembling the shape of a shuriken. The resulting substrate generates superchiral fields that neither individual component produces. The mechanism underlying this anomalous response arises from two distinct effects: first, the shuriken structures generate substantial intrinsic optical chirality; second, the nanoporous network adds densely distributed plasmonic hotspots and an interference cross-term, which augments the local chirality even more prominently. This chiral plasmonic nanoporous network achieves not only ultrasensitive chiral detection by reaching the attomole range, but also introduces enantiospecific photochemical reactivity on a single substrate under continuous-wave linearly polarised light. Raman asymmetries approach the theoretical maximum ( ≈ 2), while enantiomeric excesses exceed 25%. Finally, a six-order-of-magnitude enhancement over conventional Raman optical activity was calculated.

candidates.title: Structure-guided design of a dual-antigen mRNA vaccine conferring broad protection against Henipaviruses
candidates.authors: Binhe Du, Yun Peng, Hao Gu, Wei Huang, Yanfeng Yao, Ye Li, Mingqing Lu, Shuqi Xiao, Hang Liu, Ge Gao, Miaoyu Chen, Chao Shan, Jing Lu, Zhiming Yuan, Jinzhong Lin
candidates.abstract: Henipaviruses (HNVs), including Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV), are zoonotic paramyxoviruses with high case fatality rates and pandemic potential. Despite their threat, no licensed vaccines are currently available for human use. Here, we present a structure-guided mRNA vaccine strategy that overcomes key challenges in antigen stability, fusogenicity, and cross-protective efficacy. Using rationally engineered NiV F glycoproteins stabilized in the prefusion conformation, we identify a lead candidate (F-205) that abolishes syncytium formation and elicits high prefusion-specific antibody titers. Through systematic combinatorial screening, we determine that co-delivery of F-205 (NiV-M) and G (NiV-B) antigens via mRNA–lipid nanoparticles induces potent neutralizing and cellular immune responses. In stringent golden hamster challenge models, this vaccine confers complete survival against lethal NiV-M, NiV-B and HeV challenge, with viral RNA undetectable in lung, spleen and brain after NiV challenge and significantly reduced viral burden after HeV challenge. We also introduce surrogate assays to assess F conformation and fusion activity under standard biosafety conditions, enabling iterative antigen optimization without live-virus handling. This study defines a broadly protective, mechanistically informed vaccine platform for HNVs and provides a generalizable framework for rational design of mRNA vaccines targeting class I fusion viruses. The authors develop a structure-guided mRNA vaccine combining two Nipah virus proteins. All vaccinated hamsters survive challenge with Nipah-Malaysia, Nipah-Bangladesh or Hendra virus, with reduced viral burden.

candidates.title: Interstitial proton buffering enables decoupled transfer dynamics for acidic wastewater decontamination
candidates.authors: Minghao Xu, Yingji Zhao, Jianwen Zhang, Huawei Hu, Chengcheng Tian, Norman C.-R. Chen, Xiangyang Liu, Lei Zhou, Yusuke Yamauchi
candidates.abstract: The remediation of aggressive acidic wastewater is fundamentally hindered by the coupled proton-release/electron-transfer barrier that suppresses high-valent metal-oxo chemistry in conventional advanced oxidation processes. Here we report an interstitial proton-buffering strategy in which boron is incorporated into a cobalt-manganese phosphide lattice, guiding self-limited reconstruction into a stable oxyhydroxide interface. The interstitial B-regulated interface acts as a local Brønsted-base proton buffer, establishing a proton-acceptor–electron-donor mechanism that enables decoupled proton-electron transfer, as supported by a super-Nernstian E1/2-pH response. This pathway stabilizes CoIV-oxo formation and drives complete imidacloprid degradation within 3 min in simulated water. In 80 h continuous-flow treatment of electroplating acid-pickling wastewater at pH 0.85, the system retains 49.48% total organic carbon reduction. These results identify interstitial proton buffering as a route to sustain high-valent oxidation chemistry in strongly acidic water matrices. Strong acidity stifles high-valent metal-oxo chemistry in water purification. Here, the authors show that interstitial boron in cobalt-manganese phosphide buffers protons and decouples proton-electron transfer, sustaining oxidation below pH 2.

candidates.title: The evolutionary plateau of efflux-mediated drug resistance in mycobacteria
candidates.authors: Shiksha Sharma, Asis Kumar Khuntia, Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, Sarika Mehra
candidates.abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Bacterial genomes encode a large repertoire of multidrug efflux pumps, which could theoretically combine to achieve exceptionally high levels of resistance. To delineate the extent of resistance achievable through efflux driven adaptation, we performed adaptive laboratory evolution of Mycobacterium smegmatis mc²155 wild-type and efflux-deleted (ΔlfrA, ΔefpA) strains against ethidium bromide, a broad-spectrum efflux substrate. Despite prolonged selection, resistance reproducibly plateaued at 8-16 fold increase in MIC under the tested conditions. This plateau emerged through distinct evolutionary trajectories characterized by non-overlapping efflux pump sets: from overexpression of the well-characterized lfrA to upregulation of multiple uncharacterized pumps, all conferring cross-resistance. Genetic reconstruction of mutations in a transcriptional regulator and a membrane protein, together with overexpression of efflux pumps, recapitulated the resistance phenotypes of the evolved strains. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance. Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria. Here, Sharma et al. use experimental evolution in mycobacteria and show that, after prolonged selection, drug resistance achieved through efflux pump overexpression reaches a stable level, apparently due to exhaustion of cellular energy.

candidates.title: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
candidates.authors: Kaustubh Chakradeo, Alexandros Katsiferis, Neil Scheidwasser, Iwona Hawryluk, Katherine E. Battle, Swapnil Mishra, David L. Smith, Seth Flaxman, David A. Duchêne, Samir Bhatt
candidates.abstract: Abstract Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Stalled progress and funding constraints raise important questions about the dependence of current malaria burden on sustained intervention coverage. Here, we estimate malaria transmission potential under a low-intervention scenario where major malaria interventions are withdrawn while broader ecological and demographic conditions remain constant. We develop a contrastive representation-learning framework applied to 30-m Landsat 8 satellite imagery, integrating the resulting environmental representations within a Bayesian hierarchical model. This approach improves predictive accuracy over existing covariate-based malaria mapping methods. Using contemporary Global Burden of Disease 2024 population estimates, we estimate an annual malaria burden of 422 (275-582) million cases across sub-Saharan Africa, representing a 131% increase relative to current estimates. These findings quantify the structural vulnerability of malaria control gains across sub-Saharan Africa and reveal where intervention disruption could have the greatest impact.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Ceramics usually exhibit inherent brittleness at room temperature due to their strong covalent/ionic bonding and few active slip systems. Consequently, ceramics exhibit a low damage-bearing capacity and typically sudden failure prior to yielding. Thus, achieving room-temperature plasticity while maintaining or enhancing the strength of ceramics remains critical and challenging. Here, we report a promising strategy to address this problem by concurrently activating twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in a monolithic TaN ceramic film. Through precisely controlled physical vapor deposition, we stabilize the metastable δ-TaN phase with hierarchical nanotwinned architectures. Then, by combining micromechanical tests, atomic-resolution characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the synergy of phase transformation and twinning brings exceptional damage tolerance and plasticity, achieving up to 60% compressive strain without catastrophic fracture alongside a hardness of ~43 GPa. Our work not only proves the feasibility of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity synergy in designing ultrahard and ductile materials, but also highlights the architecture optimization in nanotwinned ceramics.

candidates.abstract: Abstract The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

candidates.title: Numerosity is directly sensed and dynamically transformed in the human brain
candidates.authors: Alireza Karami, Elisa Castaldi, Evelyn Eger, Martin N. Hebart, Manuela Piazza
candidates.abstract: Humans can estimate the number of objects in a scene within a fraction of a second, suggesting that numerosity is encoded rapidly and directly by the visual system. Yet how this encoding unfolds over time and interacts with other visual features remains unclear. Here, we combined magnetoencephalography (MEG) with time-resolved representational similarity analysis (RSA) and MEG–fMRI fusion to track how numerosity is represented in the brain over time. We also used multidimensional scaling (MDS) to visualize the evolving patterns of neural activity. Two main findings emerged. First, numerosity exhibited the hallmarks of a primary perceptual attribute: its neural signature appeared very rapidly after stimulus onset, preceding the encoding of non-numeric features that could otherwise define number. Second, multidimensional scaling of the neural manifolds revealed a temporal shift in representational geometry: an early linear structure, consistent with a summation-based code and predominant in occipital regions, transitioned into a curvilinear structure characteristic of numerosity-tuned coding, emerging more prominently in associative areas along the dorsal stream. Together, these findings demonstrate that numerosity processing is encoded directly from the visual image and unfolds through a rapid hierarchical transformation, from a broad quantity signal to a finely tuned, number-specific code, linking perceptual encoding to higher-level numerical abstraction. Brain recordings show that humans sense how many objects are in a scene almost instantly and directly, not by combining cues like size or spacing, with this number sense sharpening over the following milliseconds.

candidates.title: Evolutionary plasticity of bacterial surface layer protein exoskeletons
candidates.authors: Anna Barwinska-Sendra, Paula S. Salgado, Kacper M. Sendra
candidates.abstract: Abstract All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Prokaryotic surface layer (S-layer) exoskeletons, with their homopolymer paracrystalline architecture, offer a more tractable model of an environmental interface. However, extreme sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation of S-layer proteins confound conventional evolutionary analyses. Here, by combining phylogenomics with structural modelling, we show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across both monoderm ( Bacillaceae , Peptostreptococcaceae ) and diderm ( Caulobacteraceae , Deinococcaceae ) bacteria. Focusing on the Gram-positive order Peptostreptococcales , including environmental isolates and clinical pathogens, we uncover multiple S-layer architectures conferring divergent physiological properties. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile . Our findings establish the S-layer as a paradigm of molecular modularity and evolutionary plasticity. Specifically, evolution of a single structural protein enables rapid cell-surface reconfiguration and contributes to immune evasion in bacterial pathogens.

candidates.authors: Sanju Luhach, Tim K. Schramm, Jan Kachnowicz, Andreas Hansen, Demyan E. Prokopchuk
candidates.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a commodity chemical used broadly in the industrial sector that heavily relies on the 80+-year-old anthraquinone process, requiring significant energy input in combination with precious metal-catalyzed hydrogenation. We describe a metal-free molecular cyclopentadiene-iminium electrocatalyst for producing H2O2 under ambient conditions with high Faradaic efficiency (> 99%) and turnover frequency up to 104 s−1, surpassing some of the most active transition-metal-based molecular catalyst systems. One-electron reduction of the dication [CpN3H]2+ generates a radical cation [CpN3H]+• that becomes a potent hydrogen atom (H•) donor to O2, operating through an unusual radical-rebound mechanism to form a key hydroperoxyl intermediate ([CpN3OOH]+•). This proposed pathway is rigorously supported by cutting-edge computational and experimental mechanistic analyses. Overall, this work demonstrates an innovative and sustainable molecular approach to furnish a valuable commodity chemical through an electrically driven process without the need for transition metals. candidates.title: Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
candidates.authors: Amy Heshmati, Sol P. Juárez
candidates.abstract: Abstract Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers’ mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers’ mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

candidates.abstract: Abstract A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. We apply a global food system model to project the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1) uptake to 2050 among people with obesity under two scenarios: reduced calorie intake while maintaining dietary composition, and reduced calorie intake combined with shifts towards the EAT–Lancet diet. Compared with the Reference scenario, GLP-1-mediated calorie reduction alone results in up to 6.6 million avoided deaths globally in 2050 and 32 Mha more natural land area, reflecting reductions in cropland, pasture and managed forest. Combining GLP-1 use with EAT–Lancet dietary shifts increases these estimates to 7.7 million avoided deaths and 46 Mha more natural land. Lower food prices increase food consumption among untreated populations, including unhealthy foods, partially offsetting these gains.

candidates.title: Coherence toroidal vortices and statistic-veiled correlation topologies
candidates.authors: Keyu Zhou, Yaning Zhou, Ao Zhou, Zhao Zhang, Jinzhan Zhong, Houan Teng, Chunhao Liang, Qiwen Zhan, Yangjian Cai, Xu Guo, Xin Liu
candidates.abstract: Abstract Toroidal vortices in fluid and gas dynamics underpin a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields, from elementary particle physics to condensed matter systems, and have recently garnered significant attention in optics because of their inherent topological stability. Here we report the experimental observation of toroidal vortices in stochastic optical wavefields with partial coherence, termed coherence toroidal vortices, which eliminates deterministic topological signatures in conventional optical degrees of freedom while unveiling statistically hidden correlation topologies. These underlying topologies—including both fundamental and higher-order hopfionic textures—emerge in second-order field correlations and are accessible only through statistical measurements. We further examine the impact of chaotic channels on the stability of these statistically veiled correlation topologies, demonstrating that their topological invariants remain robust under realistic environmental perturbations. These findings are experimentally validated and offer novel insights into the potential of toroidal light vortices serving as controllable channels for directional energy and information transfer within complex media.

candidates.abstract: Abstract The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

candidates.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
candidates.authors: Samuel E. Barnett, Ashley Shade
candidates.abstract: Abstract Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

candidates.authors: Carmen V. Apostol, Ramakrishnan Anish, Son Pham, Khalil Ettayebi, Janam J. Dave, Frederick H. Neill, Marina Bok, Banumathi Sankaran, Sue E. Crawford, Robert L. Atmar, James E. Crowe Jr, Viviana Parreño, Mary K. Estes, B. V. Venkataram Prasad
candidates.abstract: Virus capsids are metastable assemblies with an exquisite balance between stability and flexibility, obligatory for entry, infectivity, and immune escape. Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. GII.4 HuNoVs have been evolving epochally, driving most global pandemics, and since 2012, GII.4 Sydney has been the dominant variant. The major capsid protein, VP1, is central to infectivity and immune recognition, and VP1-based virus-like particles (VLPs) are considered promising vaccine candidates. Yet, how the icosahedral HuNoV capsid responds to antibody pressure at the atomic level remains unclear. Here, we present the first atomic structure of GII.4 Sydney capsid determined by cryo-EM, revealing the structural features that likely contribute to its sustained dominance. Using focused refinement, we uncover the remarkable capsid plasticity in response to symmetry-breaking binding of neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies. VP1 adopts 11 distinct conformational modalities to accommodate asymmetric antibody binding, and antibody-disrupted VLPs reassemble into smaller particles with five additional VP1 states. This previously unrecognized extent of conformational adaptability provides key insights for designing next-generation VLP- or mRNA-based vaccines targeting HuNoV infections. This manuscript by Apostol and Anish et al. describes how the pandemic human norovirus capsid undergoes various conformational modalities to accommodate binding of neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies to hidden epitopes.

This polar–tropical atmospheric teleconnection strengthens monsoon circulation and moisture convergence, producing wetter conditions across the Sahara–Sahel. These results reveal a high-latitude pathway through which slow cryospheric changes modulate low-latitude monsoon variability under sustained warming.

candidates.title: Quantum sensing-enabled deuterium NMR spectroscopy with nanoscale sensitivity at low magnetic fields
candidates.authors: Dileep Singh, Riley W. Hooper, Christoph Findler, Utsab Banerjee, Dominik B. Bucher
candidates.abstract: Abstract Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unparalleled access to molecular structure and dynamics but is traditionally limited by weak signal strength, requiring large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. Here, we demonstrate nanoscale deuterium ( 2 H) NMR spectroscopy using nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, yielding characteristic quadrupolar powder line shapes that are present in conventional bulk NMR spectra. By detecting statistical spin fluctuations from nanometer-scale detection volumes, our approach delivers a sensitivity enhancement of seven to eight orders of magnitude in terms of spin sensitivity over inductive detection, while operating at magnetic fields two orders of magnitude lower than those used in conventional NMR. Temperature-dependent measurements of a deuterated polymer and a molecular solid reveal distinct motional averaging and phase transitions with nanoscale sensitivity. Powder-like NV-detected 2 H NMR establishes a powerful tool for probing molecular dynamics on the nanoscale - capabilities beyond those of most existing spectroscopic techniques.

candidates.title: Droplet-Assisted Growth of Re-Entrant Micro-Mushroom Surfaces with Switchable Superhydrophobicity and Adhesive Resistance
candidates.authors: Kangwei Chen, Marino Kriftner, Marc Frey, Nina Vonlanthen, Alexandre Laroche, Jie Xu, Stefan Seeger
candidates.abstract: Abstract Nature-inspired designs for surface micro- and nanostructures have long attracted attention for their potential multifunctionality. This study introduces a mushroom-shaped silicone re-entrant structure achieved through a one-step, in-situ dynamic Droplet-Assisted Growth and Shaping strategy. The unique shape and multicomponent hybrid properties of the inert rod base and chemically modifiable spherical head of these silicone micro-mushrooms (SMMs) provide exceptional surface wetting and adhesion characteristics. The engineered single-scale rough surface exhibits the remarkable rose petal effect, featuring a water contact angle exceeding 150° and demonstrating extraordinary water adhesion. The wetting states of these surfaces can be easily altered through O 2 -plasma treatment with the reconstruction of secondary and tertiary hierarchical nanostructures. This approach also effectively converts petal-effect surfaces into lotus-effect surfaces, significantly enhancing their self-cleaning performance. Furthermore, the SMM coatings display extremely low adhesion to various adhesives, including tapes, hot glue, and all-purpose adhesives, with pull-off forces nearing 0. This characteristic ensures a smooth detachment from sticky surfaces. The durability of the SMM structures is noteworthy, as they maintain their morphology even after 1,000 loop tack tests and can endure 8.7 MPa compression and 500 cycles of linear abrasion on sticky surfaces.

candidates.title: Bordetella pertussis adapts to human nasal mucosa through biofilm-associated virulence reprogramming and host-defense attenuation
candidates.authors: Jessica L. Gutiérrez-Ferman, Matthew I. McFadden, Rachael E. Rayner, Sahil Mahajan, Hannah M. Smith, Alexa R. Aubrey, Phylip Chen, Mohamed A. Wahba, Haitao Wen, Purnima Dubey, Daniel J. Wozniak, Mark E. Peeples, Estelle Cormet-Boyaka, Adriana Forero, Rajendar Deora
candidates.abstract: Current acellular pertussis vaccines fail to control the burden of Bordetella pertussis (Bp) in the human nasopharynx, a reservoir for transmission. To better understand the unique host and bacterial signatures in the nasal microenvironment, we inoculated primary human nasal epithelial cultures (HNEC) with Bp. Bp adhered and replicated robustly on cilia forming structured and matrix-encased biofilms. HNEC-associated biofilms were more resistant to killing by the antimicrobial peptide, LL-37, compared to abiotic biofilms and planktonic cells. Profiling of the host and bacterial mRNA signatures during infection revealed the differential regulation of host genes encoding mucins and downregulation of those involved in mucociliary clearance, epithelial barrier integrity, and host immunity. Measurement of mucins revealed an initial reduction followed by a sharp increase in MUC5AC and MUC5B, and the presence of mucin-embedded Bp biofilms. A striking downregulation of Bp genes encoding virulence factors, including all the components of current acellular pertussis vaccines, metabolic pathways; and upregulation of genes encoding iron acquisition pathways and the Bps polysaccharide was uncovered. Bps was critical for Bp-HNEC interaction and biofilm formation. Our results reveal biofilms as a potential source of Bp carriage and transmission, the cascade of host-pathogen transcriptional events during nasal infection and targets for vaccine development. Here, authors show how Bordetella pertussis forms protective biofilms on human nasal epithelium, rewires host-pathogen gene expression, reduces the production of vaccine-antigens and virulence factors.

candidates.title: A metal ion-assisted workflow for practical and scalable enrichment of small extracellular vesicles from biofluids
candidates.authors: Shuai Qiu, Junjie Xia, Wanhua Li, Xuefei Yu, Shuaihang Chen, Yuanqiang Li, Qinglin Li
candidates.abstract: Small extracellular vesicles hold immense diagnostic and therapeutic potential, yet clinical translation is hindered by inefficient separation and concentration. Current methods like ultracentrifugation and polymer-based precipitation suffer from low throughput or persistent contaminants. Here, we develop an optimized workflow that adapts the well-established binding between transition metal ions (copper(II), manganese(II), zinc(II)) and membrane phosphate groups to induce vesicle aggregation that facilitates small extracellular vesicle recovery from urine, blood and cell culture-conditioned medium using conventional centrifugation. We elucidate how buffer composition (albumin, phosphate, and hydron) and small extracellular vesicle surface properties (surface charge, phospholipid content) modulate these ion-vesicle interactions. By optimizing protocols using copper(II) for blood, zinc(II) for urine and cell culture-conditioned medium, we achieve higher yields than ultracentrifugation and polymer-based precipitation while preserving vesicle ultrastructure, molecular markers, biological function and safety. Thus, we establish a practical and scalable workflow that accelerates extracellular vesicle-based translational research. Efficient isolation of small extracellular vesicles is key for clinical applications. Here, the authors develop IonNet, a metal ion-assisted workflow that enables practical and scalable enrichment of functional small extracellular vesicles from biofluids via conventional centrifugation.

candidates.title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
candidates.authors: Shan Feng, Hexige Wuliji, Ruifeng Liu, Xinba Yaer, Xiaoping Niu, Jun Wang, Kunpeng Zhao, Hexi Baoyin
candidates.abstract: Abstract Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. However, early-stage formation of passivating oxide shells severely restricts oxygen diffusion, resulting in incomplete oxidation and limited energy utilization. Here, we report a Ce-assisted microstructure design strategy to overcome this long-standing diffusion barrier by constructing three-dimensional oxygen-diffusion scaffolds within aluminum-based fuels through trace cerium addition. Rapidly solidified Al– x Ce powders develop an interconnected Al 11 Ce 3 network, which subdivides the Al matrix into fine domains. During heating and combustion, this Al 11 Ce 3 network is preferentially oxidized into a CeO 2- x /CeO 2 -containing scaffold before extensive Al oxidation, thereby providing continuous oxygen-transport pathways into the particle interior. As a result, Al– x Ce alloy powders exhibit shorter ignition delay, faster flame propagation, shorter combustion duration, and more complete oxidation than pure Al. This work establishes a general and scalable design principle for enhancing metal-fuel combustion through rare-earth-enabled oxygen-diffusion networks.

candidates.title: Lanthanide-dependent methanotroph thrives on radioactive promethium
candidates.authors: Philippe de Bary, Robin Steudtner, Helena Singer, Björn Drobot, Andreas S. Klein, Pia Kahle, Cathleen Zeymer, Thomas Kormoll, Huub J. M. Op den Camp, Lena J. Daumann
candidates.abstract: Abstract Lanthanides serve as essential cofactors in the methanol dehydrogenases of methylotrophic bacteria. While biological function has been characterized for the naturally occurring members of the series, promethium, the only lanthanide existing as exclusively radioactive isotopes and virtually absent from nature, has remained unexplored. Here, the acidophilic methanotroph Methylacidiphilum fumariolicum SolV grows on β⁻-emitting Pm-147 as its sole lanthanide source, removing 98% of the isotope from the medium over 60 h despite a calculated radiation dose of 3.6 Gy. Reconstituted methanol dehydrogenase of the type XoxF -MDH displays Pm-dependent activity precisely between the neodymium and samarium variants. Bacterial lanthanide metabolism thus incorporates a naturally absent and radioactive member of the lanthanide series.

candidates.title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
candidates.authors: Shishuang Zhang, Huadong Tian, Jiajun Li, Zhikao Li, Jingyi Wang, Wei Sun, Hans-Jürgen Butt, Lei Xie, Hongbo Zeng
candidates.abstract: Friction at solid-liquid interfaces is typically interpreted through classical contact mechanics, but molecular origins of gas-bubble friction in aqueous environments remain elusive. Here we report the direct quantification of gas-bubble friction at solid surfaces using atomic force microscopy with nanonewton resolution. We show that bubbles enter a contact-line friction regime only after film-mediated attachment, with static and kinetic responses that reflect contact-line pinning and sliding. On octadecyltrichlorosilane-grafted substrates, friction varies non-monotonically with surface hydrophobicity, peaking at intermediate hydrophobicity due to enhanced chemical heterogeneity. Surface chemistry and nanostructure further regulate energy dissipation, with relatively low friction on uniformly rough polydimethylsiloxane-grafted surfaces. Oxygen bubbles generate higher friction than air, nitrogen and carbon dioxide bubbles, as supported by molecular dynamics simulations that implicate gas-specific intermolecular interactions in contact-line dissipation. These findings provide molecular-level insight into gas-bubble friction, with implications for friction-tunable interfaces in catalysis, microfluidics, and medical applications. Zhang et al. report the interfacial mechanisms governing bubble friction on solids, demonstrating how surface structure, chemistry, and gas identity regulate bubble mobility. These insights advance friction tunable interfaces in bubble transport.

candidates.title: Early face-experience deprivation leads to long-lasting deficits in macaque cortical face processing
candidates.authors: Saloni Sharma, Margaret S. Livingstone
candidates.abstract: Abstract Experience-dependent plasticity in early sensory cortex is restricted to critical periods early in development. Whether plasticity in higher-order cortex is similarly restricted remains unclear. In the primate ventral visual stream, face-selective cortex emerges with experience during development, providing a powerful system to test how the timing of experience shapes higher-order representations. Using three male rhesus macaques selectively deprived of early face experience followed by prolonged normal face exposure, we found that face-experience-deprived monkeys acquire face-directed viewing behavior and neural face selectivity. However, they showed atypical within-face viewing patterns, while their neural representations retained lasting signatures of early deprivation, including selectivity for both faces and hands and reduced discrimination for face identity, expression, and viewpoint. Thus, higher-order visual cortex remains plastic beyond early development, yet the timing of experience fundamentally constrains the refinement of later-acquired neural representations.

candidates.title: Combinatorial Approach to Circuit Complexity: From Approximate Quantum Codes to Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints
candidates.authors: Jinmin Yi, Ruizhi Liu, Zhi Li
candidates.abstract: Approximate quantum error correction (AQEC) provides a versatile framework for both quantum information processing and probing many-body entanglement. We reveal a fundamental tension between the error-correcting power of an AQEC and the hardness of code state preparation. More precisely, through a novel application of the Lovász local lemma, we establish a fundamental tradeoff between local indistinguishability and circuit complexity, showing that orthogonal short-range entangled states must be distinguishable via a local operator. These results offer a powerful tool for exploring quantum circuit complexity across diverse settings. As applications, we derive stronger constraints on the complexity of AQEC codes with transversal logical gates and establish strong complexity lower bounds for W state preparation. Our framework also provides a novel perspective for systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis type constraints.

candidates.title: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method
candidates.authors: Daniel Pook-Kolb, Dotan Gazith, Colin J. Clark, Erik Agrell, Barak Zackay, Bruce Allen
candidates.abstract: Pulsars are difficult to discover via γ -ray pulsations because typically only one photon is observed per ∼ 10 8 rotations. We report the first γ -ray pulsar discovered with an extension of a recently proposed algorithm, which uses efficient tools for identifying short vectors in high-dimensional lattices instead of exhaustively searching for periodic signals. PSR J1622 − 7204, an isolated pulsar spinning at 261 Hz, was found in 15 years of Fermi-LAT data using about ten CPU hours. In contrast, the previous state-of-the-art (a semicoherent search) failed after ∼ 600 CPU years. This new approach may enable the discovery of many new γ -ray pulsars, including in binary systems, a previously intractable problem without detailed prior knowledge of the orbital parameters.

candidates.title: Universal Scaling Function for Giant-Graviton Operator Product Expansion Coefficients
candidates.authors: Miao He, Yunfeng Jiang
candidates.abstract: We consider the large-spin limit S → ∞ of the operator product expansion (OPE) coefficient for two maximal giant gravitons and a spinning operator with finite twist in planar N = 4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Up to an overall normalization factor, this OPE coefficient exhibits a power-law scaling of the form S d ( g ) . We provide strong evidence that the exponent d ( g ) is free from finite-size corrections. Consequently, the all-loop asymptotic expression for the OPE coefficient can be used to determine d ( g ) exactly. We compute a conjectural expression for the scaling function d ( g ) for arbitrary values of the ’t Hooft coupling g . At weak coupling, our result agrees perfectly with the available field-theoretic results up to three-loop order. At strong coupling, we present the first three orders as concrete predictions. We further provide the finite-coupling result and show that it interpolates smoothly between the weak- and strong-coupling regimes.

candidates.title: Odd-Parity Magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard Model from Topological Exciton Condensation
candidates.authors: Rintaro Eto, Johannes Knolle
candidates.abstract: Collective excitations in condensed matter can carry nontrivial topology and provide information about quantum phases beyond their ground-state properties. At the same time, the recent emergence of altermagnetism and related nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states raises the question of how unconventional magnetic symmetry is encoded in their collective excitations. Here, we uncover a continuous evolution from topological excitons to odd-parity magnons across an interaction-driven magnetic transition in the paradigmatic Haldane-Hubbard model. In the paramagnetic phase, our newly found sharp topological excitons soften and condense into a collinear Néel state, where they evolve into Goldstone magnons displaying characteristic f -wave spin splitting. The topology of these collective modes is tied to the underlying electronic topology, such that an electron bandgap closing enforces a magnon bandgap closing, changing the magnon topology. Our results establish a direct connection between topological collective excitations and nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splittings, with potential realizations in Floquet-driven materials and cold atomic gases.

candidates.title: Spatiotemporal Quantum Advantages for Rare-Event Sampling
candidates.authors: Akshat Gupta, Jianjun Chen, Chengran Yang, Mile Gu, Caterina Doglioni, Jayne Thompson, Thomas J. Elliott
candidates.abstract: In a world fraught with uncertainty, it behooves us to consider the most disastrous possible outcomes, in order that we can best mitigate against them. Often these are extreme risk events–of high consequence, but low probability. Yet, the rarity of such events limits our ability to study them; there is a paucity of past occurrences to draw upon, and sampling such rare events from models is typically costly in time. Here, we introduce an approach for rare-event sampling based on quantum stochastic models. This integrates the memory advantages of quantum stochastic modeling—and its associated efficient means of preparing quantum sample states—with the “speedups” of quantum amplitude amplification, to yield simultaneous reductions in spatial and temporal computational complexity compared to classical Monte Carlo–based approaches.

candidates.title: Asymmetric and Scalable Electronic Hysteresis Induced by Ratchet-like Charge Injections in van der Waals Heterostructures
candidates.authors: Linshang Chen, Rui Mei, Heng Wu, Zhengyu Su, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Lili Wang, Xuewei Cao, Zhongming Wei, Ping-Heng Tan, Kostya S. Novoselov, Yanmeng Shi
candidates.abstract: Anomalous ferroelectric-like electronic hysteresis has recently been reported in intrinsically nonpolar graphene/hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) heterostructures and widely exploited to realize electrically switchable superconductivity, correlated insulators, and neuromorphic functionalities. The origin of this anomalous hysteresis is still under debate, hindering its applications. Among the proposals are moiré-driven charge transfer, twist angles between hBN, conductive sliding ferroelectricity and dielectric defects. Here we study the detailed hysteretic transport properties in dual-gated hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures. Two devices that share the same moiré and twist angle configurations exhibit strikingly distinct hysteretic responses, allowing us to unambiguously rule out moiré-induced and twist-angle-related mechanisms. Moreover, the ratchet-like charge injections give rise to unconventional hysteresis that is pronouncedly asymmetric and continuously scalable with the sweeping range of external electric fields, in sharp contrast to conventional ferroelectric behavior with fixed coercive fields that is symmetric with respect to zero field. These observations challenge the theoretical scenario in terms of spontaneous interlayer electrical polarizations and lead us to consider the defects within hBN flakes. Our analysis and simulations suggest that the interplay between the defects and conducting channel plays an important role in inducing the ratchet-like charge injections and anomalous hysteresis. Our work provides more insight in the origin of electronic hysteresis in graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures, and the observations of asymmetric and scalable electronic hysteresis could lead to new-generation ultrafast memory and synaptic devices.

candidates.title: Topological Multicomponent Superconductivity with Sizable s -Wave Admixture in Twisted Bilayer Cuprates
candidates.authors: Yu-Hang Li, Congjun Wu, Wang Yang
candidates.abstract: We investigate multicomponent superconductivity in twisted bilayer cuprates with order parameter s + d 1 e i ϕ 1 + d 2 e i ϕ 2 , where s = s 1 + s 2 is the layer-symmetric s -wave pairing and d i is the d -wave pairing in layer i . When ϕ 1 − ϕ 2 ≠ 0 , π , this three-component state spontaneously breaks time-reversal and C 4 rotational symmetries and can realize a topologically nontrivial phase. Ginzburg-Landau analysis and self-consistent mean-field calculations show that this state is stabilized over a broad parameter regime. We further identify nematic Kerr anisotropy as a key signature distinguishing it from s + i d and d 1 + e i ϕ d 2 , and find that its Josephson critical current remains sizable near the 45 ∘ twist. Our results show that s -wave pairing does not preclude chiral topological superconductivity, pointing to twisted cuprates as a more robust platform than previously appreciated.

candidates.title: Surface-Induced Vortex Core Restructuring in a Spin-Triplet Superfluid
candidates.authors: Riku Rantanen, Mikael Huppunen, Erkki Thuneberg, Vladimir Eltsov
candidates.abstract: Observing the structure of quantized vortices can provide evidence for the pairing nature of a superfluid or superconductor and pinpoint its order parameter. Spin-triplet superfluid 3 He supports a variety of vortices, calculated and identified so far in bulk fluid. We show numerically that the vortex core in 3 He is strongly altered near a surface, resulting in a structure inhomogeneous along the vortex line. The effect is asymmetric with respect to the relative orientation of the core order parameter anisotropy axis and the surface normal. Coupling of spin and orbital degrees of freedom in the gradient energy of a triplet order parameter allows the surface to lift the degeneracy of two bulk vortex states connected by spontaneously broken inversion symmetry of the core. In a wide range of external conditions, the vortex structure at the surface is found to be completely different from that in bulk. As an implication, surface-limited vortex core observations in a triplet-candidate system may not reflect the bulk structure. We propose an experimental verification of the effect by measuring a transition in the vortex structure in thin slabs of superfluid 3 He-B.

candidates.title: Maximum Velocity of a Liquid Metal Drop Driven by a Time-Dependent Electrocapillary Excitation
candidates.authors: Javier Otero Martinez, Ana Garcia Armada, Yi Li, Christian A. Nijhuis, Javier Rodríguez Rodríguez
candidates.abstract: Gallium alloys are promising materials in biomedical engineering, electronics, and wireless communications, thanks to their good conductivity and their ability to sustain large deformations. They can be transported in capillaries using continuous electrowetting (CEW). Current models of CEW-driven flows do not address the transient response to fast changes in the excitation voltage, crucial in many applications. Here, we study the CEW-driven oscillatory motion of a drop of a Gallium alloy inside a capillary. We consider inertia, viscosity and the transient response of the electrical circuit consisting of the drop plus the electrolyte where it is immersed. The theory describes fairly well the experimental drop velocity and explains the existence of an optimal frequency that maximizes the velocity.

candidates.title: Topological Quantum Criticality in the Quasiperiodic Cluster Ising Chain
candidates.authors: Sheng Yang, Hai-Qing Lin, Xue-Jia Yu
candidates.abstract: Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have recently attracted growing interest, as they go beyond the traditional paradigms of condensed matter and statistical physics. However, such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic environments, particularly under quasiperiodic modulations. In this Letter, we uncover a family of topological quasiperiodic fixed points with critical scalings intermediate between the clean and infinite-randomness limits. By exactly solving the quasiperiodic cluster Ising chain, we demonstrate that all phase boundaries separating quasiperiodically modulated phases are governed by topological Ising-like fixed points unique to strongly modulated quasiperiodic systems. Although their local bulk critical properties match those of conventional quasiperiodic Ising critical points reported before, these fixed points host robust topological edge degeneracies and exhibit a distinct symmetry-enriched realization of the quasiperiodic Ising criticality, as further supported by complementary lattice simulations.

candidates.title: Origin of Electride States and Their Responses under Pressure
candidates.authors: Xuefen Cai, Qiu-Shi Huang, Su-Huai Wei
candidates.abstract: Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. While existing theoretical frameworks, including the interstitial quasi-atom (ISQ) and electron-ion interaction (EII) models, have provided some useful phenomenological interpretations of the electride formation, the atomistic origin and the underlying physics of this charge redistribution remain unclear. Here, within a first-principles framework, we systematically study the evolution of electronic structures of compressed materials, using alkali metals as representative examples. By mapping symmetry-resolved electronic band states onto atomic orbitals, we find that (i) pressure-induced quantum confinement raises the energies of atomic orbitals due to enhanced kinetic energy and increased overlap between valence and core electrons, with the energy shift being larger for more delocalized s orbital than for more localized p and d orbitals; and (ii) this effect causes reordering of band states, making the electride states, which are composed of the interatomic hybridized pd orbitals, to progressively shift in energy below the s orbital states, leading to their occupation and the onset of electride behavior. This microscopic electronic-state picture clarifies the origin of the electride formation and provides a general framework for understanding the evolution of interstitial electronic states under compression across diverse materials.

candidates.title: Minding the Gap between Hard and Diffractive Structure Functions at the Electron-Ion Collider
candidates.authors: June-Haak Ee, Christopher Lee, Stella T. Schindler
candidates.abstract: Diffraction is characterized by forward scattering and a large rapidity gap. Ordinary hard scattering also produces gapped events and presents a significant background to identification of diffractively produced events. We present a fully differential factorization of gapped hard e p scattering. We find that the unpolarized azimuthally dependent structure functions F 3 , 4 gap and the longitudinal F L gap vanish at leading power for hard scattering. Azimuthal dependence is thus a pure diffractive signature. This is borne out in Monte Carlo simulations.

candidates.title: Rectification at High Currents in Asymmetric Two-Dimensional Electron Structures: Electron Tesla Valve
candidates.authors: Daniil I. Sarypov, Dmitriy A. Pokhabov, Arthur G. Pogosov, Evgeny Yu. Zhdanov, Andrey A. Shevyrin, Askhat K. Bakarov
candidates.abstract: In solids, frequent electron-electron collisions can induce collective, fluid-like electron transport. While this regime offers a powerful framework for exploring many-body phenomena, there is still a lack in functional electronic device actively exploiting hydrodynamic behaviour of electrons. Here, we introduce a solid-state analogue of a Tesla valve — a passive fluidic diode that rectifies flow without moving parts. Lithographically defined in high-mobility GaAs two-dimensional electron gas, the device exhibits abrupt rectification producing a more than tenfold difference between forward and reverse resistances. This threshold behaviour, reminiscent of the onset of turbulence in fluidic Tesla valves, points to the emergence of turbulent regime in the electron liquid — a long-predicted, but yet unobserved state of electronic matter. More broadly, our work demonstrates the fruitfulness of the hydrodynamic analogy: fluidic technologies can be readily adopted to create novel electronic devices. Here, this is realized through a solid-state rectifier whose operation relies on a new physical mechanism, interparticle collisions.

candidates.title: Interaction-Induced Sign Reversal of the Orbital Magnetic Susceptibility in Chern Insulators
candidates.authors: Ke Huang, Xiao Li
candidates.abstract: It has been well established that the orbital magnetization of interacting electrons can be simply evaluated by applying the single-particle formula to self-consistent Hartree-Fock (HF) bands. However, we show that such a procedure fails qualitatively for orbital magnetic susceptibility, especially in topological systems: in a Chern-insulating phase of twisted MoTe 2 , the interaction-induced correction reverses the sign of the susceptibility. This result follows from an algebraic framework that solves the HF problem at finite magnetic field, where noncommuting canonical momenta obstruct a direct calculation: a maps every magnetic-translation-invariant operator to a unique bivariate function, converting the finite-field self-consistency into a function equation that can be expanded systematically in B . At first order, this yields a linear equation for the field-induced change δ X of the Fock potential, leading to an intrinsically interaction-induced susceptibility in addition to a single-particle-like one. The framework reproduces the Středa formula for insulators, and an auxiliary-Hilbert-space construction carries it to periodic and moiré systems. Finite-field HF calculations in a gapped Dirac model and in the twisted MoTe 2 Chern insulator confirm the theory quantitatively.

candidates.title: Input-State-Dependent Chiral State Transfer Enabled by Iso-Imaginary Riemann Surfaces
candidates.authors: Kai Hong, Jian Wang, Andrea Alù, Lin Chen
candidates.abstract: Encircling exceptional points (EPs) in non-Hermitian systems has been shown to induce chiral state transfer, whereby the final state of the system is always the lowest-loss eigenstate, independent of the input. When multiple lowest-loss states coexist, it is generally expected that EP encirclement yields mixed outputs composed of these states. Here we reveal a distinct regime, peculiar of non-Hermitian systems hosting multiple iso-imaginary Riemann surfaces, extending the conventional understanding of EP dynamics. We find that states residing on higher-loss Riemann surfaces preferentially undergo nonadiabatic transitions to the nearest lower-loss surface, while transitions between iso imaginary surfaces are strongly suppressed. This fixed-selection-rule dynamics enables input-state-dependent chiral transfer, such that encircling the same EP produces distinct and well-defined output states for different inputs, rather than mixed output states. We experimentally demonstrate this mechanism in a photonic platform, revealing new EP dynamics beyond conventional chiral state transfer, and opening a pathway towards mode-selective, high-capacity non-Hermitian photonic devices.

candidates.title: Extracting Central Charge from Ground-State Overlaps of Spatially Deformed Hamiltonians
candidates.authors: Chen Bai, Xinyu Sun, Liang-Hong Mo, Hong-Hao Tu
candidates.abstract: We show that the conformal anomaly of a ( 1 + 1 ) -dimensional conformal field theory can be extracted directly from a ground-state wave-function overlap associated with a spatial conformal deformation. Focusing on the q -M"obius deformation, we derive an exact overlap formula between the deformed and undeformed ground states, whose exponent directly encodes the central charge. Motivated by this result, we construct a lattice estimator based solely on ground-state overlaps and apply it to representative critical quantum chains and the gapless edge modes of a two-dimensional Chern insulator. Numerical results demonstrate that the resulting overlaps provide a simple and robust probe of the central charge in microscopic models. We further demonstrate that the deformed ground states retain universal geometric structures in their entanglement spectra and entanglement entropies. These results provide a simple wave-function-based route to probing conformal data in critical systems and topological edge modes.

candidates.title: Evidence for Clean d -Wave Superconductivity in the Samarium Nickelates
candidates.authors: Qingming Huang, Xiaofang Fu, Junlong Wu, Laifeng Li, Liang Qiao, Ye Yang
candidates.abstract: The discovery of superconducting nickelates provides a unique opportunity to explore the pairing mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. Here, we use ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy to probe the temperature-dependent superfluid density in an infinite-layer samarium nickelate film with a T_c of 20 K. The superfluid density decreases linearly with rising temperature, consistent with clean-limit d-wave pairing in cuprate superconductors. From this linear relation, we extract a superconducting gap Δ(0) = 2.5 ± 0.1 meV and a gap-to-T_c ratio, 2∆(0) /k_B T_c≈3, suggesting that this sample lies in the weak-coupling regime. Furthermore, the ratio of the mean free path to the coherence length, l/ξ, is determined to be ~1.5, confirming clean-limit behavior. These findings suggest strong parallels between the pairing mechanisms in nickelate and cuprate superconductors.

candidates.title: System Size Dependence of Collisionless Reconnection Rate
candidates.authors: Yi-Min Huang, Naoki Bessho, Li-Jen Chen, Judith T. Karpen, Amitava Bhattacharjee
candidates.abstract: It is a widely accepted paradigm that collisionless magnetic reconnection proceeds at a universal fast rate of ∼ 0.1 when normalized to a properly defined reconnecting magnetic field and Alfv'en speed, effectively independent of the macroscopic system size. This conclusion, derived primarily from kinetic simulations of classical Harris current sheets with kinetic-scale thickness, stands in contrast to results from forced reconnection and island coalescence, where the rate significantly depends on the system size. Here, we reconcile this disparity by performing a rigorous scaling study of Harris sheets using both particle-in-cell and Hall magnetohydrodynamic simulations. We demonstrate that when the global magnetic configuration is preserved by scaling the initial current sheet thickness proportionally with the system size, the "universal" fast rate disappears. Instead, the reconnection rate decreases as the system size increases. By establishing a consistent scaling trend across different magnetic configurations, these findings challenge the paradigm of scale-independent fast reconnection and necessitate a reevaluation of energy release rates in astrophysical plasmas.

candidates.title: Scalable Generation of Macroscopic Fock States Exceeding 10,000 Photons
candidates.authors: Ming Li, Weizhou Cai, Ziyue Hua, Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Zi-Jie Chen, Xu-Bo Zou, Guang-Can Guo, Luyan Sun, Chang-Ling Zou
candidates.abstract: The scalable preparation of bosonic quantum states with macroscopic excitations poses a fundamental challenge in quantum technologies, limited by control complexity and photon-loss rates that severely constrain prior theoretical and experimental efforts to merely dozens of excitations per mode. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its effcacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. candidates.authors: Michael A. Perlin, Zichang He, Anthony Alexiades Armenakas, Pablo Andres-Martinez, Tianyi Hao, Dylan A. Herman, Yuwei Jin, Karl Mayer, Chris N. Self, David Amaro, Ciaran Ryan-Anderson, Ruslan Shaydulin
candidates.abstract: Scaling up quantum algorithms to tackle high-impact problems in science and industry requires quantum error correction and fault tolerance. We further show that QAOA circuits with up to eight logical qubits and nine logical T gates perform similarly to unencoded circuits. For the largest QAOA circuits we run, with 12 logical (97 physical) qubits and 2132 physical two-qubit gates, we still observe better-than-random performance. Finally, we show that adding active quantum error correction cycles and increasing the repeat-until-success limit of state-preparation subroutines can improve the performance of a quantum algorithm, thereby demonstrating critical capabilities of scalable FT quantum computation. Our results are enabled by a FT logical T -gate implementation with an infidelity of 2.7 ( 4 ) × 10 − 3 and dynamic circuits with measurement-dependent feedback. candidates.abstract: The efficient preparation of scalable multipartite entanglement is a central goal in the development of next-generation quantum devices. In this work, we show that the so-called “twist-and-turn” (TaT) dynamics for interacting spin ensembles, generated by Hamiltonians with U(1)-symmetric interactions and with a transverse field, can offer an important resource to reach this goal. For models with sufficiently high connectivity, TaT dynamics exhibits two key features: (1) It features both scalable squeezing at short times, as well as quantum Fisher information with Heisenberg scaling at later times, and (2) scalable multipartite entanglement (up to Heisenberg scaling) is reached in a time growing only logarithmically with system size, associated with an exponential buildup of quantum correlations. For dipolar interactions, the entanglement dynamics at intermediate times is completely at odds with thermalization, and it appears to saturate the maximum speed of entanglement buildup allowed by Lieb-Robinson bounds generalized to power-law interacting systems.

candidates.abstract: Antiferromagnets with broken time-reversal symmetry, including altermagnets, have attracted growing interest because they can exhibit ferromagnet-like responses, such as the anomalous Hall effect and magneto-optical effects, despite their compensated spin structures. Such time-reversal symmetry breaking is characterized by ferroic time-reversal-odd multipoles, distinct from the conventional spin and orbital moments. Among them, the anisotropic magnetic dipole (AMD), which reflects the local orbital anisotropy, shares the symmetry of magnetization and can have a ferroic component even when the spin moments cancel. AMD responses have thus far been identified primarily in antiferromagnets with unit-cell magnetic periodicity, whereas spatially modulated AMDs in long-wavelength magnetic textures remain unexplored. Here, we report resonant soft x-ray small-angle scattering measurements on the antiferromagnetic spin cycloid of the multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. We observe pronounced circular dichroism in the resonant scattering intensity, i.e., scattering circular dichroism, which is not expected from the established cycloidal and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-interaction-induced sinusoidal spin structures. We show that the staggered rotation of the FeO$_6$ octahedra gives rise to ferroic AMD components despite the antiparallel spin alignment. As the local magnetic symmetry varies with the cycloidal phase, these AMDs are spatially modulated and produce the dichroism through interference with the sinusoidal spin component. Our findings demonstrate that long-wavelength antiferromagnetic textures can host spatially modulated AMDs, opening new avenues for exploring hidden multipole textures in magnetic and multiferroic materials.

candidates.abstract: We report a high-precision experiment on measuring the low-frequency magnetic field reflected from a metallic plate. This experiment is designed to give insight into why theoretical predictions of the fundamental Lifshitz theory using the standard response function to the electromagnetic waves are in contradiction with the data of numerous precision measurements of the Casimir force (the Casimir puzzle). To attain these ends, we measured the magnitude and phase of the lateral component of the magnetic field produced by an oscillating magnetic dipole and reflected from a metallic plate. These quantities are completely determined by the evanescent waves with the transverse electric (s) polarization. The obtained measurement data are compared with theoretical predictions using the standard Drude response function of the metal to the low-frequency electromagnetic waves. It is shown that there are both quantitative and qualitative disagreements with these predictions, so that in the region of low-frequency s-polarized evanescent waves the Drude response function is excluded by the data. Keeping in mind that just the s-polarized evanescent waves are responsible for the Casimir puzzle, our results highlight the causes for its emergence. It is emphasized that, in addition to the Casimir effect, searching for the adequate nonlocal response functions of metals to the evanescent waves is of utmost significance for many areas of physics as near-field optical microscopy, nanophotonics, surface plasmon polaritons, radiative heat transfer, and others.

candidates.abstract: A neural network that learns an inverse map inherits the approximations of the forward solver used to generate its training data. We demonstrate this in the inference of spin Hamiltonians from synthetic neutron-scattering spectra and show how a fast many-body solver can overcome the limitation of linear spin-wave theory (LSWT). We consider a family of anisotropic triangular-lattice spin Hamiltonians at fields just above saturation, where magnon interactions shift and broaden the spectrum in ways that LSWT cannot capture. Using the truncated Hilbert-space ladder (THL) method, we compute the dynamical spin structure factor (DSSF) nonperturbatively within the one- and two-magnon space. THL is fast enough to generate large training sets of DSSF spectra, enabling us to train neural networks that accurately predict Hamiltonian parameters. By empirically benchmarking several neural-network architectures, we find that a one-dimensional convolutional network performs best. A learned forward decoder then reconstructs the DSSF from the predicted parameters, providing a rapid self-consistency check and a visualization of the predicted response. When interactions are strong, networks trained on LSWT and THL spectra infer markedly different parameters. Analysis of the Fisher information matrix shows that the measurement protocol, including which spin-correlation components are resolved and the momentum cut, determines which couplings can be identified. Combining machine learning with fast many- body theory is therefore essential for quantitative Hamiltonian inference from scattering data.

candidates.abstract: Dephasing is widely expected to induce diffusion in quasiperiodic lattices due to the loss of phase coherence. However, this expectation can fail dramatically in lattices possessing singular onsite potentials or vanishing hoppings which are expected to trivially localize the particle. Remarkably, we show that the transport in such lattices can be subdiffusive under proper conditions for which the "mean resistance" of the lattice diverges. As a result, we obtain a transition from diffusive to subdiffusive transport depending on the strength of quasiperiodic modulation. candidates.abstract: In quantum many-body physics spectral statistics is often used as a probe to distinguish integrable and chaotic models. We find a special case of an integrable spin chain with unusual spectral properties. With open boundary conditions the model has homogeneous exponential degeneracies; these are split for periodic boundary conditions. In the latter case, we find that a small number of sectors (selected by a global symmetry) showcase Wigner-Dyson spectral statistics, which usually signals quantum chaos. Our model is clean, translationally invariant, and it fits into the standard Yang-Baxter framework. We identify Hilbert space fragmentation as the key mechanism behind the spectral properties. The fragmentation is non-local, and its extent is different in the case of open and periodic boundary conditions. We argue that the dynamics of the model is not chaotic despite the unusual spectral correlations.

Using wave-function overlaps between a Chern band and freely chosen reference states, we show that crystalline symmetry can enforce their zeros and fix their vorticities modulo the rotation order from the angular momenta of the band and reference state. candidates.abstract: Metastable decay in first-order phase transitions proceeds through the nucleation of critical droplets. In the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising chain, the cost of the two walls bounding a droplet is independent of its size. For interactions decaying as $1/r^{1+σ}$, this surface cost instead depends on the droplet size and competes with the bulk free-energy gain. The critical radius scales as $R_c\propto h^{-1/σ}$ at small $h$, where $h>0$ is the bias field. The value $σ=1$ separates two regimes: for $σ 1$, it remains finite, as in the nearest-neighbor chain. A nonlocal $φ^4$ field theory yields critical droplets with algebraic tails and confirms the predicted radius and barrier scalings, while stochastic long-range dynamics independently reproduces the critical-radius scaling.

Using an ab initio many-body approach, we study crystalline tellurium (Te), a strongly anharmonic helical crystal. These symmetries protect the circular polarization of vibrational modes at finite temperature but not their lifetimes such that the dynamic chirality of handed vibrational modes persists to 600 K, even as lifetimes drop sharply. When the Majorana localization length $ξ_F$ exceeds the vortex core size $ξ$, nearby vortices acquire an additional short-range attractive channel from Majorana hybridization, modifying the vortex-antivortex interaction at short distances and generating a metastable minimum in the two-vortex free energy above the nominal $T_{BKT}$. We propose an array of Josephson-coupled $p+ip$ superconducting islands as a microscopic platform realizing the required hierarchy of scales. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures of this first-order transition, in particular a hysteresis loop whose width is set by the coexistence window.

candidates.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. With hole doping the response recovers, and at densities reachable by electric double-layer gating CsPbI3 attains the spin Hall conductivity of p-GaAs. The response is therefore determined by the position of the halide-p bands relative to the valence band maximum, not by the atomic spin-orbit constant, a criterion that applies to any semiconductor with an orbital-singlet band edge. These results point to CsPbI3 as a candidate gate-controlled source of spin current for perovskite spin-orbit torque devices.

candidates.abstract: The ability to measure thermal properties and visualize heat transport processes with high spatial resolution is becoming increasingly important for materials discovery, next-generation electronics, and advanced manufacturing. As critical dimensions and architectures of novel materials and high performance electronics shrink and become more heterogeneous, thermal transport is no longer governed by bulk material properties alone, but by local variations in microstructure, such as interfaces and defects, while the operating conditions can also play a role. With the development of non-contact pump-probe thermoreflectance techniques, specific heat, thermal conductivity, and interface conductance can be mapped either through wide-field thermos-reflectance images or by scanning technique. However, key challenges remain such as the balance between imaging throughput and measurement accuracy, the extraction of multiple parameters with high confidence, and non-intrusive subsurface characterization, etc. This Review highlights recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI)-assistance in high-throughput data processing, visualizing interfacial thermal transport, and nonintrusive subsurface analysis, and offers outlooks for future research directions such as spectral mapping of heat carriers, three-dimensional property mapping, and AI-agentic experimental designs. We anticipate this Review will motivate future efforts in combining AI with experimental techniques to achieve unprecedented capabilities for thermal characterization of nanoscale materials and device characterization, facilitating materials discovery and electronics revolution.

candidates.abstract: An important step towards the practical implementation of spin-orbit torque magnetic memory is the field-free switching of the magnetization vector. In this work, we investigate spin-orbit torque-driven magnetization dynamics and switching devices comprising monolayer $\mathrm{WTe}_2$ as the spin-source material. We perform a comparative analysis of the two phases of $\mathrm{WTe}_2$, namely the $1\mathrm{T}_d$ and $1\mathrm{T}'$ with the necessary symmetries for field-free deterministic magnetization switching. We demonstrate switching in both systems and analyse the dependence of the switching dynamics on the applied bias voltage, ribbon orientation and width of the magnetic layer. Modelling the ferromagnet as an exchange-coupled macrospin within a non-equilibrium Green's function framework, we find that the $x$-ribbon geometry of the $1\mathrm{T}_d$ $\mathrm{WTe}_2$ phase generates a significantly larger current-induced spin polarization than the $1\mathrm{T}'$ phase, resulting in a larger damping-like torque on the adjacent magnetic layer and faster switching. The switching time of $1\mathrm{T}'$ devices varies strongly and non-monotonically with the width of the magnetic layer. In $1\mathrm{T}_d$ devices, it remains nearly constant over a broad range of widths, consistent with an edge-dominated torque.
